channel.title: Clisa Geopolitics
channel.description: A geopolitical dashboard analyzing Northeast Asian security, great-power competition, and conflicts in Europe and the Middle East from South Korea’s vantage point. Each issue comes with a situation assessment, a strategy evaluation, what it means for people, and probabilistic forecasts.

item.title: Briefing · October 15, 2026
item.description: Ukraine's air force counts 39 Russian missiles and 128 drones; 600,000 lose power · Russia's Defense Ministry claims strikes on six power plants around Kyiv and Kharkiv · North Korea test-fires two types of submarine-launched strategic cruise missiles in the East Sea · Singapore-flagged container ship sinks in Strait of Hormuz after projectile strike · Houthis claim they targeted Riyadh's King Khalid airport; coalition intercepts ballistic missile · U.S. consumer prices rise 3.7 percent in September as gasoline jumps 34.2 percent

item.title: Briefing · October 13, 2026

item.title: Forecast review · October 12 · 4 revised, 2 unchanged
item.description: Last week the United States allowed supplies of Russian diesel, but Russia stayed away from a U.S.-led meeting, and Iran kept the strait closed, calling the U.S. reply insufficient. The probabilities of four forecasts were lowered, and two forecasts with conflicting factors were left unchanged.

item.title: Issues · Issue change: AI and Chips removed, Russia-NATO standoff added
item.description: The AI and Chips issue has been removed from the issues under analysis, and a new issue has been published: "The Russia-NATO standoff: How should Poland prepare for the Russian threat?" Forecasts f46–f53, which are tied to the AI and Chips issue, will remain until their resolution dates.

item.title: Features · What it took for a country to invent an alphabet
item.description: A third feature, "What it took for a country to invent an alphabet," was published for Hangul Day. It traces the two conditions, one domestic and one external, that sustained King Sejong's 32-year reign: where they came from and why they lasted only a generation. It then puts the same question to the Korean Peninsula of 2026.

item.title: Forecast review · October 5 · 4 revised, 2 unchanged
item.description: Last week the United States sent more forces to the Middle East, raising the military pressure on Iran, and North Korea fired a hypersonic intermediate-range missile while rejecting inter-Korean contact. The probabilities of four forecasts were adjusted, and two forecasts with conflicting factors were left unchanged.

item.title: Features · South Koreans' well-being hangs by a thread
item.description: A second feature based on population projections, "South Koreans' well-being hangs by a thread," has been published. The October 1 feature has been retitled "The security vacuum the Korean Peninsula can expect in the 2030s."

item.title: Features · The security vacuum the Korean Peninsula can expect in the 2030s
item.description: One key assessment and four forecasts (f54–f57) were added to the Korean Peninsula issue. They address the mismatch between the pace at which the United States is handing South Korea primary responsibility for deterring North Korea and the pace at which South Korea is acquiring the means to carry that responsibility.
